documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of EGM
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: SK Minerals & Additives reported a 50% revenue growth in FY26 to Rs. 318 crores, with EBITDA margins rising to 10%. The company is expanding into polymer additives, specifically halogen-free flame retardants, and plans to invest Rs. 20 crores in CAPEX over FY27 and FY28. Management aims to increase manufacturing's revenue contribution from 23% to 50% over the next two to three years while scaling total capacity to 18,000 metric tons.

guidance.claim: The company aims to scale the revenue contribution of manufacturing to 50% in the next two to three years.
guidance.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

guidance.claim: The company expects margins from polymer additives to be around 40%.
guidance.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%.

guidance.claim: The company expects the polymer additives plant to be fully utilized in the next six months.
guidance.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

guidance.claim: The company plans to file three patents in the next six months.
guidance.quote: But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

demand_outlook.claim: The company is currently focusing on the cable and wire and electrical and electronics equipment industries for its flame-retardant products.
demand_outlook.quote: This flame-retardant is being used in various industries, but currently, we are focusing on cable and wire and electrical and electronics equipment.

demand_outlook.claim: The company plans to target EV batteries once it caters to the cable, wire, and electrical equipment segments.
demand_outlook.quote: Once we cater to these two segments, then we will target EV batteries also.

demand_outlook.claim: The company is receiving queries for its flame-retardant product from international buyers.
demand_outlook.quote: As currently, we are getting a few queries from the international buyers also.

capex_expansion.claim: The company is looking to increase its total capacity to 18,000 metric tons in a phased manner over the next 18 months.
capex_expansion.quote: Basically, we are looking at total capacity of 18,000 metric tons including all the current capacity and this we are going to increase in the phased manner in the next 18 months.

capex_expansion.claim: The company acquired a 9.6 acre land to develop its polymer additives and polymer compound facility.
capex_expansion.quote: First of all, this 9.6 acre land which we have taken is for developing our polymer additives and polymer compound facility, whereas specified that in next 12 to 18 months, we will be taking our manufacturing capabilities to 18,000 metric tons.

margins_costs.claim: The company's EBITDA margins increased from 9% to 10% and PAT increased from 5% to 6% in the last financial year.
margins_costs.quote: Our financial performance, which is last financial year we have closed is Rs. 318 crores we have closed and this is 50% growth from the Financial Year ‘25 and our EBITDA margins have increased from 9% to 10% and PAT has increased from 5% to 6%.

margins_costs.claim: Margins declined in the second half of FY26 due to an increase in raw material prices starting from January.
margins_costs.quote: It is because of the increase in the prices of raw materials. And as I have said prices have increased specifically, from January onwards, the prices of raw material have increased.

margins_costs.claim: The company's gross margin from manufacturing is currently 30%, while trading gross margin is 21%.
margins_costs.quote: So, in terms of gross margin, which we make from manufacturing, right now it's 30%. Whereas, in terms of our trading product, it is 21%.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's current order book is around Rs. 55 crores.
orders_capacity.quote: Currently, order book is around about Rs. 55 crore and it depends upon the customer.

orders_capacity.claim: Out of the Rs. 55 crores order book, Rs. 42 crores is from government contracts.
orders_capacity.quote: Out of these Rs. 55 crores, Rs. 42 crores is from government and rest is from private.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's current installed capacity is 6,600 metric tons, with an overall capacity utilization of 70%.
orders_capacity.quote: The current capacity is 6600 metric tons. And as we have added polymer additives, which is 450 metric tons per month, which is going to live in the next three months. So, the current capacity is 70%.

orders_capacity.claim: The food and feed segments are running at 95% capacity utilization.
orders_capacity.quote: Food and feed is being running at 95%, and the polymer additive industry is yet to get live in the next three months.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volume grew from 33,000 metric tons in FY25 to 46,000 metric tons in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: So, the volume was 33,000 metric ton in FY25 and this year it was 46,000 metric ton in 2026, which comprises of 4,400 metric ton of manufacturing capabilities.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's current working capital cycle is 110 days, and it is working to reduce it to improve cash flows.
capital_allocation.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is of 110 days. We are trying to reduce this working capital cycle because it will improve in cash flow also in the organization.

capital_allocation.claim: The company plans to fund its CAPEX using bank credit lines and IPO proceeds.
capital_allocation.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical scenarios have impacted import trading as the company's three-month stock is getting dried up.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of the import trading, yes, it has impacted because we have three months’ stock always available with us. So, that stock is getting dried up.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company's polymer additives plant is experiencing teething problems.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

risks_headwinds.claim: Raw material prices increased tremendously in February.
risks_headwinds.quote: So, we have sourced the material for next six months or suddenly there was demand from December onwards of these raw materials and the prices have increased tremendously in February of these raw materials.

management_commitments.claim: The company wants to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50% in the next two to three years.
management_commitments.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

management_commitments.claim: The company will try to file three patents in the next six months.
management_commitments.quote: But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

management_commitments.claim: The company will try to address teething problems in the polymer additives plant in the next three months.
management_commitments.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
